text:
Predicates:
WorksInStudentJobs(x) ::: x works in student jobs on campus.
OrderTakeoutFrequently(x) ::: x orders takeout frequently in college.
EnjoysDiningHallMeals(x) ::: x enjoys the dining hall meals and recipes.
PickyEater(x) ::: x is a picky eater.
SpendTimeEatingAndCatchingUp(x) ::: x spends a lot of their time eating and catching up with friends in the campus dining halls.
NeedsMoneyForTuition(x) ::: x needs to earn money to help pay for their college tuition.
Hannah ::: Hannah is at Mary's school.

Premises:
∀x (WorksInStudentJobs(x) → NeedsMoneyForTuition(x)) ::: If people work in student jobs, they need money for tuition.
∀x (OrderTakeoutFrequently(x) → WorksInStudentJobs(x)) ::: If people order takeout frequently, they work in student jobs.
∀x (OrderTakeoutFrequently(x) ∨ (EnjoysDiningHallMeals(x) ∧ Recipes(x))) ::: People either order takeout frequently or enjoy dining hall meals and recipes.
∀x (EnjoysDiningHallMeals(x) → ¬PickyEater(x)) ::: If people enjoy dining hall meals, they are not picky eaters.
∀x (EnjoysDiningHallMeals(x) → (SpendTimeEatingAndCatchingUp(x))) ::: If people enjoy dining hall meals, they spend a lot of time eating and catching up with friends.
Hannah ::: Hannah is at Mary's school.
WorksInStudentJobs(Hannah) ::: Hannah works in student jobs on campus.
(NeedsMoneyForTuition(Hannah) → (¬PickyEater(Hannah) ∧ NeedsMoneyForTuition(Hannah))) ::: If Hannah needs to earn money, then she is not picky and needs money.

Conclusion:
NeedsMoneyForTuition(Hannah) ::: Hannah needs to earn money to help pay for her college tuition.
